$comment: The hand-curated half of the wickedagile.com graph: threads, Related links, map positions, short map labels, the door names and the hero. Essays come from the Medium feed, bits and videos from bits.wickedagile.com/bits.json, Work facts from the lab's export (src/lib/sources.mjs); topic edges are computed from the essays' own Medium categories by scripts/build-graph.mjs. Everything here is an operator choice.

topicEdgeRule.shape: chain in date order, newest first

threads.name: Start here
threads.hook: You can now build the wrong solution ten times faster than you could a year ago.

evidence.quote: You can now build the wrong solution ten times faster than you could a year ago.

threads.name: What if everything is green?
threads.hook: Three parables about the confidence that comes from drawing a firm line, finding a pattern, and seeing everything green.

the confidence that comes from finding a pattern

threads.name: Who checks the work?
threads.hook: Code is cheap. Confidence isn’t: knowing what correct means is still the hard part.

evidence.quote: The Hard Part Is Still Knowing What Correct Means
Independent review had to become structural

threads.name: How far does reality travel?
threads.hook: Proximity changes what you notice, and the real work begins before anyone opens an IDE.

evidence.quote: How Far Does Reality Have to Travel?
The real work begins before anyone opens an IDE.

threads.name: What survives the screen?
threads.hook: The interface changes. The state survives. So what would you lose if you deleted the screen?

evidence.quote: The interface changes. The state survives.
If I deleted its interface tomorrow, what would stop us from rebuilding the useful parts?
A release is a controlled transition between valid system states.

essayIds.$comment: Medium post id (the hex at the end of the post's link, which a title edit keeps) -> the essay's id here; a post not listed takes its link's slug

threadsDraft: DRAFT FOR OPERATOR APPROVAL: thread names, hooks and membership are proposals (threads are curated, R6).

layout.$comment: grid units: Learn sky columns 0..6.6, rows 0..5.0; Work stations sit on a fixed right shore (rows only). Label sides are chosen so that no route ever leaves a station on its label's side. Learn items without a position (a new essay) take the next free tray slot; beyond the tray they appear in the Learn list only.

approvalRule: A thread or Related link is shown as approved only with "approval": {"by": "operator", "on": "YYYY-MM-DD"}; until then it carries "draft": true.

minsOverride.$comment: essay id -> {mins, source}; a read time the feed snapshot couldn't give. Coord default for DES Q10 (2026-11-03); the operator can override.

the-last-engineer.source: Medium full-RSS copy (medium.com/feed/@mike.parcewski, built 2026-11-03): 786 words at 230 wpm, rounded like the feed's other read times; the article page refuses scripts (403), so Medium's own read time was not compared

labels.$comment: the two doors' public names; change here to swap Work for Do or Build

hero.$comment: DECIDED by the operator 2026-11-02 (option 1). 'Receipts' is the family's word for a job's evidence: the hero promises no more than the receipts show. Earlier drafts A-C are in DES §13.3.
hero.h1: We write about the work. The tools are the receipts.
hero.sub: Essays and interactive pieces on AI and how software gets built, each one a thread into the wicked tools that do the work and keep the record.
